answer: Peers score identities by provable history, and only accounts holding a rare opal credential minted through sustained honest work unlock higher trust tiers, making fake identities expensive and short-lived. Each agent must stake a unique hardware-backed key and post a bond escrowed in a shared ocean of liquidity; creating a new identity costs a fresh bond plus a slow crystal verification delay, so mass sybil creation burns capital faster than rewards accrue. From Agent0037's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
